title: SCRANTIC.SCR name-table aliasing makes a small file decode into unbounded sound memory at startup
description: NeFile::wave_resources decodes a WAVE resource into a fresh Vec<f32> for every RT_NAMETABLE entry named WAVESFX<n>, even when many entries point at the same (type id, resource id), and keeps each copy in ExeData::sounds. A crafted SCRANTIC.SCR with one large WAVE and thousands of ~19-byte name entries allocates ~4 x WAV size per entry at startup (ScreensaverData::load), before the first frame, causing OOM abort or host memory pressure; with the .scr this repeats on every idle launch. Soft-audio resampling (always on in the .scr) compounds it per played id.
root_cause: wave_resources has no per-resource or aggregate budget on decoded samples and no deduplication by (type_id, res_id); decoded output is O(name entries x WAV size) rather than O(file size).
intended_behavior: Decoded sound memory bounded by a constant budget (comparable to MAX_UNPACKED) or linearly by distinct WAVE bytes; aliases share one decoded buffer; over-budget input rejected with AssetError::Format.

trace.description: ScreensaverData::load_first loads SCRANTIC.SCR at startup (also .scr /s and /p).
Whole file read via read_ci/fs::read, no size cap, then ExeData::parse.
Resource offset/len are u16<<shift (shift<=15); one WAVE can be as large as the file.
Name-table loop runs once per entry with no entry or byte budget.
sounds.insert(n, decode_wav(wav)?) re-decodes the aliased resource per entry; every copy retained.

evidence.description: resources.get(&(type_id, res_id)) lets any number of names resolve to one resource; no dedup.
Each decode collects a new Vec<f32> sized to the data chunk.
ExeData::sounds: HashMap<u32, Vec<f32>> owns each copy for the program lifetime.
Soft mode resamples and caches per id (~17.4 bytes per WAV byte at 48 kHz).

conditions.description: User installs a crafted SCRANTIC.SCR (third-party abandonware sources) and runs the program, or Windows launches the .scr on idle.
Crafted NE passes the build-string check (ACTIVITY.ADS at DS:0x1681, WAVESFX%d at DS:0x1D56) and minimal table layout.

execution.attacker_perspective: Supplier of SCRANTIC.SCR controlling all its bytes, no other access.
payloads: Synthetic 14-segment NE (build(n, wav_len) in agents/hunter-exe/artifacts/alias-evidence.txt): resource table shift 4 with name table type 0x800F id 0x8001 and one RIFF/WAVE type 0x8011 id 0x8002 (64 KiB of 0x80); name table holds N entries [len, 0x8011, 0x8002, "\0WAVESFX<k>"].
instructions: Compile alias.rs in sandbox-run.sh against the harness rlib (unchanged src/assets), rustc --edition 2024 -C opt-level=3 -C overflow-checks=off -C panic=abort.
Run `alias N 65536` for N in 1 16 64 256 1024; it prints file size, sounds, retained f32 bytes, time, VmHWM.
Stop at the growth curve; extrapolate retained = N x 4 x WAV size.

remediation.strategy: Decode each distinct (type_id, res_id) once and share it; enforce an aggregate decoded-sample budget (like MAX_UNPACKED) and reject over-budget files; optionally cap single-WAVE length; add a regression test with many aliasing WAVESFXn names expecting Err.

likelihood.reason: Victim must install a crafted SCRANTIC.SCR from a third-party source; no network vector.

impact.reason: Local availability only: startup OOM abort or host memory pressure; .scr fails on every idle launch until the file is removed; no memory corruption.

confidence.reason: Unchanged parser exercised in release-equivalent profile; memory grew linearly with name entries from a fixed small file.
